verdict.rationale: Calendly supports Workflows (automated pre/post-meeting emails/texts, reminders, reschedule requests) and webhooks that fire real-time payloads on scheduling/cancellation events, giving trigger→action automation; routing forms also apply conditional logic to route bookings. However, these are pre-built, fairly rigid automation primitives (fixed trigger types, template-based actions) rather than a flexible rules engine where an AI-native user can define arbitrary custom conditional logic across many event types. missing for 10: evidence of a general-purpose rules/conditions builder (if-this-then-that style with custom logic beyond routing forms/workflows), user-defined triggers beyond the fixed webhook/workflow event set, and independent/hands-on confirmation that Workflows or webhook automation reliably deliver in practice.
